# onpager_work_calendar (Resource)

Manage one work calendar's settings independently of its entries.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "onpager_work_calendar" "example" {
  team_id = var.team_id
  name    = "Office hours"
  # With provider timezone = "Europe/Moscow", these local clocks become
  # 06:00Z through 14:00Z. Source weekday identities remain UTC.
  base_schedule = {
    reference_date = "2024-01-01"
    intervals = [
      { starts_at = "2024-01-01T09:00:00", ends_at = "2024-01-01T17:00:00" },
      { starts_at = "2024-01-02T09:00:00", ends_at = "2024-01-02T17:00:00" },
      { starts_at = "2024-01-03T09:00:00", ends_at = "2024-01-03T17:00:00" },
      { starts_at = "2024-01-04T09:00:00", ends_at = "2024-01-04T17:00:00" },
      { starts_at = "2024-01-05T09:00:00", ends_at = "2024-01-05T17:00:00" },
    ]
  }
  working_weekend_schedule = {
    reference_date = "2024-01-01"
    intervals      = []
  }
  inherit_production_calendar = false
  production_country_code     = "RU"
}

variable "team_id" {
  description = "Existing owning team UUID."
  type        = string
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name unique case-insensitively within this team among non-retired calendars. Must be nonempty without leading or trailing whitespace.
- `team_id` (String) Owning team UUID. Changing it replaces this resource. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID.

### Optional

- `base_schedule` (Attributes) Dated weekly intervals. Omission or `null` on creation uses the API 24x7 default; on later applies it retains server settings. Explicit `intervals = []` creates or clears all weekly working hours. Source weekdays remain UTC. Use exact minute precision; at most 16 normalized intervals per source UTC day. The backend validates source-week bounds and canonicalizes local-midnight fragments. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--base_schedule))
- `inherit_production_calendar` (Boolean) Whether production-calendar working/nonworking dates are inherited for `production_country_code`. Defaults to `false`. No production calendar is downloaded by Terraform.
- `production_country_code` (String) Existing canonical production country code. Defaults to `RU`. Must match `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_-]{1,15}$`: 2 through 16 uppercase letters, digits, underscores or hyphens, starting with a letter, without surrounding whitespace. Must be valid even when inheritance is `false`; empty and lowercase values are invalid.
- `working_weekend_schedule` (Attributes) Dated fallback intervals for production working weekends, restricted to `SA`/`SU`. Omission or `null` on creation defaults to empty; on later applies it retains server settings. Explicit `intervals = []` clears it. Source weekdays remain UTC. Use exact minute precision; at most 16 normalized intervals per source UTC day. The backend validates source-week bounds and canonicalizes local-midnight fragments. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--working_weekend_schedule))

### Read-Only

- `aggregate_revision` (Number) Aggregate revision including entries. Informational only; never used for settings or entry writes.
- `id` (String) Stable nonzero canonical lowercase OnPager UUID.
- `request_timezone` (String) Explicit provider request timezone last applied to local datetime inputs. Null when the provider timezone is omitted or all inputs have explicit offsets. Changing the explicit provider timezone plans an update for local inputs; refresh alone preserves saved instants. The backend interprets local clocks and reports DST ambiguity or nonexistent times.
- `revision` (Number) Calendar settings revision used in strong numeric `If-Match` for settings updates and archival. Independent of entry revisions; stale settings report a conflict.

### Nested Schema for `base_schedule`

Required:

- `intervals` (Attributes Set) Unordered dated windows. Use [] to clear all intervals. At most 512 windows; do not supply overlapping or touching periods. Local values use the provider request timezone; explicit offsets always identify absolute instants. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--base_schedule--intervals))
- `reference_date` (String) Fixed explicit UTC source Monday: 2024-01-01. This date is a declaration reference, independent of the current date and provider request timezone.

<a id="nestedatt--base_schedule--intervals"></a>
### Nested Schema for `base_schedule.intervals`

Required:

- `ends_at` (String) Exclusive end; same formats as starts_at and must follow it. Mixed local and explicit-offset ordering is checked by the backend.
- `starts_at` (String) Inclusive local datetime in YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss form or explicit RFC3339 instant. Sent unchanged; the backend resolves local input in the provider request timezone and rejects DST ambiguity or gaps.

## Import

Import using `team_uuid/calendar_uuid`. Import reads the calendar in the fixed
reference week and adopts explicit-offset dated windows. Configure those
returned windows to avoid changing settings after import.

Use an `import` block:

```terraform
import {
  to = onpager_work_calendar.example
  id = "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111/66666666-6666-4666-8666-666666666666"
}
```

Or use the CLI:

```shell
terraform import onpager_work_calendar.example 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111/66666666-6666-4666-8666-666666666666
```

## Lifecycle

This resource owns calendar settings. Use `onpager_work_calendar_entry` for
individual calendar entries. Settings updates do not replace entries. Updates
and archival use the settings revision; aggregate revisions are informational.
Conflicts retain state and require a new plan.

Destroy archives the calendar, preserving its UUID, entries and historical
references. Active escalation chains or enabled schedules can block archival
with `calendar_in_use`; remove their links explicitly. A confirmed archive or
direct `404 not_found` removes the resource from state. Archive restoration is
unsupported.

Production-calendar countries must exist even when inheritance is disabled. The
provider does not download production calendars.

## Dated windows and timezone

Weekly declarations use explicit dated windows with fixed source Monday
`2024-01-01`. Each schedule object contains `reference_date` and an `intervals`
set; use `intervals = []` to clear it. Weekday and working-weekend selectors
refer to UTC source days. A Sunday source window can display on local Monday.
The API validates that the supplied instants fit the fixed UTC source week.

Local `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss` inputs are sent unchanged and resolved by the API in
the provider request `timezone`. RFC3339 values with `Z` or an explicit offset
identify absolute instants. The API stores UTC, returns offset timestamps and
rejects ambiguous or nonexistent local times. Windows require exact minute
precision. The fixed reference week defines recurring UTC hours even when its
zone offset differs from another season; it does not define local-time
recurrence.

State preserves configured windows while their authoritative API instants remain
equivalent, including responses with different offsets or fragments split at
midnight. Changed intervals appear as drift. Configured windows and private
server timestamp bindings persist in Terraform state.

Changing an explicit provider `timezone` plans an update through computed
`request_timezone` when windows contain local values. Apply sends the same local
strings in the new zone; refresh preserves stored instants. Explicit-offset-only
windows do not require a write when the request zone changes. Omitted provider
timezone follows the API actor's default without explicit zone tracking.

## Permissions

Requires owning-team grants `team_work_calendars.read`,
`team_work_calendars.create`, `team_work_calendars.update` and
`team_work_calendars.delete`. Service accounts require explicit native grants.
